title: A Long Walk
description: Find the longest path through a maze with optional slope constraints.
writeup:
## Approach

The maze has long corridors connecting junction points. First condense the graph: identify junctions (cells with 3+ walkable neighbors plus start/end), then BFS from each junction to find the distance to neighboring junctions.

## Part 1

Slope tiles (`>`, `<`, `v`, `^`) force movement in one direction, making the condensed graph a DAG. DFS with backtracking finds the longest path efficiently since there are few junctions.

## Part 2

Ignore slopes, making the graph undirected. Longest path in a general graph is NP-hard, but the condensed graph has only ~36 junctions, making bitmask-based DFS with backtracking feasible. Bitwise visited tracking keeps the constant factor low.
